nodes.title: Sliced adjoint functors
nodes.text: If $a : F \vdash G$ is an adjunction between $F : C \to D$ and $G : D \to C$ and $X : C$, then there is an adjunction between $F / X : C / X \to D / F(X)$ and $G / X : D / F(X) \to C / X$.

nodes.title: Limit-preserving functors lift to over categories
nodes.text: Let $J$ be a shape (i.e. a category). Let $\widetilde J$ denote the category which is the same as $J$, but has an extra object $*$ which is terminal. If $F : C \to D$ is a functor preserving limits of shape $\widetilde J$, then the obvious functor $C / X \to D / F(X)$ preserves limits of shape $J$.

nodes.title: Essential image of a sliced functor
nodes.text: If $F : C \to D$ is a full functor between cartesian-monoidal categories, then $F / X : C / X \hom D / F(X)$ has the same essential image as $F$.

nodes.title: Fully faithful product-preserving functors lift to monoid/group objects
nodes.text: If a finite-products-preserving functor $F : C \to D$ is fully faithful, then so is $\Grp(F) : \Grp C \to \Grp D$.

nodes.title: Equivalences lift to monoid/group object categories
nodes.text: If $e : C \backsimeq D$ is an equivalence of cartesian-monoidal categories, then $\Grp(e) : \Grp(C) \backsimeq \Grp(D)$ too is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.title: Essential image of a functor on monoid/group objects
nodes.text: If $F : C \to D$ is a fully faithful functor between cartesian-monoidal categories, then $\Grp(F) : \Grp(C) \hom \Grp(D)$ has the same essential image as $F$.

nodes.title: A fully faithful functor product-preserving is a group isomorphism on hom sets
nodes.text: If $F : C \to D$ is a fully faithful functor between cartesian-monoidal categories and $X, G \in C$ are an object and a group object respectively, then $\Grp(F) : (X \hom G) \hom \backcong (F(X) \hom F(G))$ is a group isomorphism.

nodes.title: Pulling back a module object
nodes.text: Let $M, N$ be two monoid objects in a monoidal category $C$. Let $f : M \to N$ be a monoid morphism. If $X$ is a $N$-module object, then it is also a $M$-module object.

nodes.title: The tensor product of linearly independent families
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain and $M, N$ two $R$-semimodules. If $f$ and $g$ are linearly independent families of points in $M$ and $N$, then $(i, j) \mapsto f i \ox g j$ is a linearly independent family of points in $M \ox N$.

nodes.title: Multivariate Laurent polynomials are an integral domain
nodes.text: Multivariate Laurent polynomials over an integral domain are an integral domain.

nodes.title: Affine monoid
nodes.text: An \emph{affine monoid} is a finitely generated commutative monoid which is: \begin{itemize} \item cancellative: if $a + c = b + c$ then $a = b$, and \item torsion-free: if $n a = n b$ then $a = b$ (for $n \geq 1$). \end{itemize}

nodes.title: Embedding an affine monoid inside a lattice
nodes.text: If $M$ is an affine monoid, then $M$ can be embedded inside $\Z^n$ for some $n$.

nodes.title: Affine monoid algebras are domains
nodes.text: If $R$ is an integral domain $M$ is an affine monoid, then $R[M]$ is an integral domain and is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.

nodes.title: Irreducible element
nodes.text: An element $x$ of a monoid $M$ is \emph{irreducible} if $x = y + z$ implies $y = 0$ or $z = 0$.

nodes.title: Irreducible elements lie in all sets generating a salient monoid
nodes.text: If $M$ is a monoid with a single unit, and $S$ is a set generating $M$, then $S$ contains all irreducible elements of $M$.

nodes.title: A salient finitely generated monoid has finitely many irreducible elements
nodes.text: If $M$ is a finitely generated monoid with a single unit, then only finitely many elements of $M$ are irreducible.

nodes.title: A salient finitely generated cancellative monoid is generated by its irreducible elements
nodes.text: If $M$ is a finitely generated cancellative monoid with a single unit, then $M$ is generated by its irreducible elements.

nodes.title: Coideal
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $(C,\Delta,\varepsilon)$ be a coalgebra over $R$. An $R$-submodule $I$ of $C$ is a \emph{coideal} of $C$ if $\Delta(I) \subseteq \bar{I \otimes_R C} + \bar{C \otimes_R I}$ and $\varepsilon(I)=0$, where $\bar{\cdot}$ denotes the image in $C \otimes_R C$.

nodes.title: Quotient coalgebra
nodes.text: If $C$ is a coalgebra over $R$ and $I$ is a coideal, the quotient $C /I$ is equipped with a canonical $R$-coalgebra structure.

nodes.title: Quotient coalgebra map
nodes.text: If $C$ is a coalgebra over $R$ and $I$ is a coideal, the quotient map $C \to C / I$ is a coalgebra homomorphism.

nodes.title: Bialgebra ideal
nodes.text: Let $B$ be a bialgebra over a commutative ring $R$. A \emph{bialgebra ideal} $I$ is an ideal which is also a coideal.

nodes.title: Quotient bialgebra
nodes.text: If $B$ is a bialgebra over $R$ and $I$ is a bialgebra ideal, the quotient $B / I$ is equipped with a canonical $R$-bialgebra structure.

nodes.title: Quotient bialgebra map
nodes.text: If $B$ is a bialgebra over $R$ and $I$ is a bialgebra ideal, the quotient map $B \to B / I$ is a bialgebra homomorphism.

nodes.title: Hopf ideal
nodes.text: Let $A$ be a Hopf algebra over a commutative ring $R$. A \emph{Hopf ideal} $I$ is a bialgebra ideal such that $S(I)=I$.

nodes.title: Quotient Hopf algebra
nodes.text: If $A$ is a Hopf algebra over $R$ and $I$ is a Hopf ideal, the quotient $A / I$ is equipped with a canonical Hopf algebra structure over $R$.

nodes.title: Quotient Hopf algebra map
nodes.text: If $A$ is a Hopf algebra over $R$ and $I$ is a Hopf ideal, the quotient map $A \to A / I$ is a Hopf algebra homomorphism.

nodes.title: Freeness of group algebras under an injective hom
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $G, H$ be abelian groups and $f : G \to H$ an injective group hom. Then $R[H]$ is a free $R[G]$-module.

nodes.title: The kernel of a map on direct sums
nodes.text: Let $G$ be an abelian group generated by a set $S$. Let $A, B$ be arbitrary indexing types and $f : A \to B$ a function. Write $f^\oplus : G^{\oplus A} \to G^{\oplus B}$ the pushforward. Then \[ \ker f^\oplus = \Span\{gX^a_1 - gX^a_2 | g \in S, a_1, a_2 \in A, f(a_1) = f(a_2)\}. \]

nodes.title: Localising a monoid algebra
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $M$ be a commutative monoid and $M'$ be its localization at some $S \subseteq M$. Then $R[M']$ is the localization of $R[M]$ at $\Span \{X^s | s \in S\}$.

nodes.title: Group-like elements
nodes.text: An element $a$ of a coalgebra $A$ is \emph{group-like} if $\eta(a) = 1$ and $\Delta(a) = a \ox a$, where $\eta$ is the counit and $\Delta$ is the comultiplication map. We write $\GrpLike A$ for the set of group-like elements of $A$.

nodes.title: Group-like elements form a group
nodes.text: Group-like elements $\GrpLike A$ of a bialgebra $A$ form a monoid. Group-like elements $\GrpLike A$ of a Hopf algebra $A$ form a group.

nodes.title: Bialgebra homs preserve group-like elements
nodes.text: Let $f : A \to B$ be a bi-algebra hom. If $a \in A$ is group-like, then $f(a)$ is group-like too.
If $R$ is a commutative semiring, $A$ is a Hopf algebra over $R$ and $G$ is a group, then every element of the image of $G$ in $A[G]$ is group-like.
If $R$ is a commutative semiring, $A$ is a Hopf algebra over $R$ and $G$ is a group, then the group-like elements in $A[G]$ span $A[G]$ as an $A$-module.

nodes.title: Independence of group-like elements
nodes.text: The group-like elements in a bialgebra $A$ over a domain are linearly independent.

nodes.title: Group-like elements in a group algebra
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain. The group-like elements of $R[M]$ are exactly the image of $M$.

nodes.title: Galois connection between group algebra and group-like elements
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a $R$-bialgebra. Then bialgebra homs $R[G] \to A$ are in bijection with group homs $G \to \GrpLike A$.

nodes.title: Quotients by binomial ideals
nodes.text: Let $A$ be a Hopf algebra, $H$ be a subgroup of $\GrpLike A$ and \[ I = \langle h_1 - h_2 : h_1,h_2 \in H \rangle \] be an ideal. Then $I$ is a Hopf ideal.

nodes.title: Diagonalizable bialgebras
nodes.text: A bialgebra is called diagonalizable if it is isomorphic to a group algebra.
A diagonalizable bialgebra is spanned by its group-like elements.

Let $A$ be a bialgebra over a domain $R$, let $G$ be a subgroup of $\GrpLike(A)$ (which is a monoid by \ref{0-grp-like-grp}). If $A$ is generated by $G$, then the unique bialgebra morphism from $R[G]$ to $A$ sending each element of $G$ to itself is bijective.

nodes.title: Quotient of a diagonalisable bialgebra is diagonalisable
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain, $G$ a commutative group, $A$ a $R$-bialgebra and $f : R[G] \to A$ a surjective bialgebra hom. Then $R[f(G)] \cong A$ as bialgebras.
A bialgebra over a domain is diagonalizable if and only if it is spanned by its group-like elements.

nodes.title: The antipode is a antihomomorphism
nodes.text: If $A$ is a $R$-Hopf algebra, then the antipode map $s : A \to A$ is anti-commutative, ie $s(a * b) = s(b) * s(a)$. If further $A$ is commutative, then $s(a * b) = s(a) * s(b)$.

nodes.title: Bialgebras are comonoid objects in the category of algebras
nodes.text: The category of $R$-bialgebras is equivalent to comonoid objects in the category of $R$-algebras.

nodes.title: Hopf algebras are cogroup objects in the category of algebras
nodes.text: The category of $R$-Hopf algebras is equivalent to cogroup objects in the category of $R$-algebras.

nodes.title: The group algebra functor
nodes.text: For a commutative ring $R$, we have a functor $G \rightsquigarrow R[G] : \Grp \to \Hopf_R$.

nodes.title: The group algebra functor is fully faithful
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain. The functor $G \rightsquigarrow R[G]$ from the category of groups to the category of Hopf algebras over $R$ is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Convex cone generated by a set
nodes.text: For a set $S \subseteq N$, the {\bf cone generated by $S$}, aka {\bf cone hull of $S$}, is $$\Cone(S) := \left\{\sum_{u \in S} \lambda_u u | \lambda_u \ge 0\right\}$$

nodes.title: Convex polyhedral cone
nodes.text: A {\bf polyhedral cone} is a set that can be written as $\Cone(S)$ for some finite set $S$.

nodes.title: Convex hull
nodes.text: For a set $S \subseteq N$, the {\bf convex hull of $S$} is $$\Conv(S) := \left\{\sum_{u \in S} \lambda_u | \lambda_u \ge 0, \sum_u \lambda_u = 1\right\}$$

nodes.title: Polytope
nodes.text: A {\bf polytope} is a set that can be written as $\Conv(S)$ for some finite set $S$.

nodes.title: Dual cone
nodes.text: Given a polyhedral cone $\sigma \subseteq N$, its {\bf dual cone} is defined by $$\sigma^\vee = \{m \in M | \forall u \in \sigma, \langle m, u\rangle \ge 0\}$$.

nodes.title: Dual of a polyhedral cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is polyhedral, then its dual $\sigma^\vee$ is polyhedral too.

nodes.title: Dual cone of a sumset
nodes.text: If $\sigma_1, \sigma_2$ are two cones, then $$(\sigma_1 + \sigma_2)^\vee = \sigma_1^\vee \cap \sigma_2^\vee.$$

nodes.title: Double dual of a polyhedral cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is polyhedral, then $\sigma^{\vee\vee} = \sigma$.

nodes.title: Face of a cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is a cone, then a subset of $\sigma$ is a {\bf face} iff it is the intersection of $\sigma$ with some halfspace. We write this $\tau \preceq \sigma$. If furthermore $\tau \ne \sigma$, we call $\tau$ a proper face and write $\tau \prec \sigma$.

nodes.title: Edge of a cone
nodes.text: A dimension 1 face of a cone is called an \emph{edge}.

nodes.title: Facet of a cone
nodes.text: A codimension 1 face of a cone is called a \emph{facet}.

nodes.title: Face of a polyhedral cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is a polyhedral cone, then every face of $\sigma$ is a polyhedral cone.

nodes.title: Intersection of faces
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is a polyhedral cone, then the intersection of two faces of $\sigma$ is a face of $\sigma$.

nodes.title: Face of a face
nodes.text: A face of a face of a polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is again a face of $\sigma$.
Let $\tau$ be a face of a polyhedral cone $\sigma$. If $v, w \in \sigma$ and $v + w \in \tau$, then $v, w \in \tau$.

nodes.title: Dual cone of the intersection of halfspaces
nodes.text: If $\sigma = H_{m_1}^+ \cap \dots \cap H_{m_s}^+$, then $$\sigma^\vee = \Cone(m_1, \dots, m_s).$$

nodes.title: Facets of a full dimensional cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is a full dimensional cone, then facets of $\sigma$ are of the form $H_m \cap \sigma$.

nodes.title: Intersection of facets containing a face
nodes.text: Every proper face $\tau \prec \sigma$ of a polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is the intersection of the facets of $\sigma$ containing $\tau$.

nodes.title: Dual face
nodes.text: Given a cone $\sigma$ and a face $\tau \preceq \sigma$, the {\bf dual face} to $\tau$ is $$\tau^* := \sigma^\vee \cap \tau^\perp$$

nodes.title: The dual face is a face of the dual
nodes.text: If $\tau \preceq \sigma$, then $\tau^* \preceq \sigma^\vee$.

nodes.title: The double dual of a face
nodes.text: If $\tau \preceq \sigma$, then $\tau^{**} = \tau$.

nodes.title: The dual of a face is antitone
nodes.text: If $\tau' \preceq \tau \preceq \sigma$, then $\tau' \preceq \tau$.

nodes.title: The dimension of the dual of a face
nodes.text: If $\tau \preceq \sigma$, then $$\dim \tau + \dim \tau^* = \dim N.$$

nodes.title: Relative interior
nodes.text: The {\bf relative interior}, aka {\bf intrinsic interior}, of a cone $\sigma$ is the interior of $\sigma$ as a subset of its span.

nodes.title: The relative interior in terms of the inner product
nodes.text: For a cone $\sigma$, $$u \in \Relint(\sigma) \iff \forall m \in \sigma^\vee \setminus \sigma^\perp, \langle m, u\rangle > 0$$

nodes.title: Relative interior of a dual face
nodes.text: If $\tau \preceq \sigma$ and $m \in \sigma^\vee$, then $$m \in \Relint(\tau^*) \iff \tau = H_m \cap \sigma$$

nodes.title: Minimal face of a cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma$ is a cone, then $W := \sigma \cap (-\sigma)$ is a subspace. Furthermore, $W = H_m \cap \sigma$ whenever $m \in \Relint(\sigma^\vee)$.

nodes.title: Salient cones
nodes.text: A cone $\sigma$ is {\bf salient}, aka {\bf pointed} or {\bf strongly convex}, if $\sigma \cap (-\sigma) = \{0\}$.

nodes.title: Alternative definitions of salient cones
nodes.text: The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $\sigma$ is salient \item $\{0\} \preceq \sigma$ \item $\sigma$ contains no positive dimensional subspace \item $\dim \sigma^\vee = \dim N$ \end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Separation lemma
nodes.text: Let $\sigma_1, \sigma_2$ be polyhedral cones meeting along a common face $\tau$. Then $$\tau = H_m \cap \sigma_1 = H_m \cap \sigma_2$$ for any $m \in \Relint(\sigma_1^\vee \cap (-\sigma_2)^\vee)$.

nodes.title: Rational cone
nodes.text: A cone $\sigma \subseteq N_\R$ is {\bf rational} if $\sigma = \Cone(S)$ for some finite set $S \subseteq N$.

nodes.title: Faces of a rational cone
nodes.text: If $\tau \preceq \sigma$ is a face of a rational cone, then $\tau$ itself is rational.

nodes.title: The dual of a rational cone
nodes.text: $\sigma^\vee$ is a rational cone iff $\sigma$ is.

nodes.title: Ray generator
nodes.text: If $\rho$ is an edge of a rational cone $\sigma$, then the monoid $\rho \cap N$ is generated by a unique element $u_\rho \in \rho \cap N$, which we call the {\bf ray generator} of $\rho$.

nodes.title: Minimal generators
nodes.text: The {\bf minimal generators} of a rational cone $\sigma$ are the ray generators of its edges.

nodes.title: A rational cone is generated by its minimal generators
nodes.text: A salient convex rational polyhedral cone is generated by its minimal generators.

nodes.title: Regular cone
nodes.text: A salient rational polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is {\bf regular}, aka {\bf smooth}, if its minimal generators form part of a $\Z$-basis of $N$.

nodes.title: Simplicial cone
nodes.text: A salient rational polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is {\bf simplicial} if its minimal generators are $\R$-linearly independent.

nodes.title: Dual lattice of a cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma \subseteq N_\R$ is a polyhedral cone, then the lattice points \[ S_\sigma := \sigma^\vee \cap M \] form a monoid.

nodes.title: Gordan's lemma
nodes.text: $S_\sigma$ is finitely generated as a monoid.

nodes.title: Affine toric variety of a rational polyhedral cone
nodes.text: $U_\sigma := \Spec \bbC[S_\sigma]$ is an affine toric variety.

nodes.title: Dimension of the affine toric variety of a rational polyhedral cone
nodes.text: \[ \dim U_\sigma = \dim N \iff \text{ the torus of $U_\sigma$ is } T_N = N \ox_[\Z] \bbC^* \iff \sigma \text{ is salient}. \]

nodes.title: The irreducible elements of the dual lattice of a cone
nodes.text: If $\sigma \subseteq N_\R$ is salient of maximal dimension, then the irreducible elements of $S_\sigma$ are precisely the minimal generators of $\sigma^\vee$.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on algebras
nodes.text: Spec is a contravariant functor from the category of $R$-algebras to the category of schemes over $\Spec_R$.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on algebras is fully faithful
nodes.text: Spec is a fully faithful contravariant functor from the category of $R$-algebras to the category of schemes over $\Spec_R$, preserving all limits.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on bialgebras
nodes.text: Spec is a contravariant functor from the category of $R$-bialgebras to the category of monoid schemes over $\Spec_R$.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on bialgebras is fully faithful
nodes.text: Spec is a fully faithful contravariant functor from the category of $R$-bialgebras to the category of monoid schemes over $\Spec_R$.

nodes.title: Spec sends cocommutative bialgebras to commutative monoid schemes
nodes.text: If $A$ is a cocommutative bialgebra over $R$, then $\Spec A$ is a commutative monoid scheme.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on Hopf algebras
nodes.text: Spec is a contravariant functor from the category of $R$-Hopf algebras to the category of group schemes over $\Spec_R$.

nodes.title: Spec as a functor on Hopf algebras is fully faithful
nodes.text: Spec is a fully faithful contravariant functor from the category of $R$-Hopf algebras to the category of group schemes over $\Spec_R$.

nodes.title: Essential image of Spec on algebras
nodes.text: The essential image of $\Spec : \Ring_R \to \Sch_{\Spec R}$ is precisely affine schemes over $\Spec R$.

nodes.title: Essential image of Spec on bialgebras
nodes.text: The essential image of $\Spec : \Bialg_R \to \GrpSch_{\Spec R}$ is precisely affine monoid schemes over $\Spec R$.

nodes.title: Essential image of Spec on Hopf algebras
nodes.text: The essential image of $\Spec : \Hopf_R \to \GrpSch_{\Spec R}$ is precisely affine group schemes over $\Spec R$.

nodes.title: The diagonalisable group scheme functor
nodes.text: Let $G$ be a commutative group and $S$ a base scheme. The diagonalisable group scheme $D_S(G)$ is defined as the base-change of $\Spec \Z[G]$ to $S$. For a commutative ring $R$, we write $D_R(G) := D_{\Spec R}(G)$.

nodes.title: Diagonalisable group schemes
nodes.text: An algebraic group $G$ over $\Spec R$ is {\bf diagonalisable} if it is isomorphic to $D_R(G)$ for some commutative group $G$.

nodes.title: The diagonalisable group scheme torus over $\Spec R$
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an abelian monoid. Then $D_R(M)$ is isomorphic to $\Spec R[M]$.
An algebraic group $G$ over a field $k$ is diagonalizable if and only if $\Gamma(G)$ is spanned by its group-like elements.
Let $R$ be a domain. The functor $D_R(G) := G \rightsquigarrow \Spec R[G]$ from the category of groups to the category of group schemes over $\Spec R$ is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Morphisms between diagonalisable group schemes are affine
nodes.text: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $M, N$ be commutative monoids and $f : M \to N$ a monoid hom. Then the map $D_S(f) : D_S(N) \to D_S(M)$ is affine.

nodes.title: Closed embeddings between diagonalisable group schemes
nodes.text: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $M, N$ be commutative monoids and $f : M \to N$ a surjective monoid hom. Then the map $D_S(f) : D_S(N) \to D_S(M)$ is a closed embedding.

nodes.title: Faithfully flat morphisms between diagonalisable group schemes
nodes.text: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $G, H$ be abelian groups and $f : G \to H$ an injective group hom. Then the map $D_S(f) : D_S(H) \to D_S(G)$ is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: A subgroup of a diagonalisable group scheme is a diagonalisable group scheme
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain. Let $G$ be an abelian group. If $H$ is a closed subgroup of $D_R(G)$, then $H$ is a diagonalisable group scheme.

nodes.title: Diagonalisable group scheme of a torsion group is disconnected
nodes.text: Let $G$ be an abelian group with an element of torsion $n$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $n$ invertible. Then $D_R(G)$ is disconnected.

nodes.title: The split torus
nodes.text: The split torus $\G_m^n$ over a scheme $S$ is the pullback of $\Spec \Z[x_1^{\pm 1}, \dotsc, x_n^{\pm 1}]$ along the unique map $S \to \Spec \Z$.

nodes.title: Diag is a group isomorphism on hom sets
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain. The functor $G \rightsquigarrow \Spec R[G]$ from the category of groups to the category of group schemes over $\Spec R$ is a group isomorphism on hom sets.

nodes.title: Characters of a group scheme
nodes.text: For a group scheme $G$ over $S$, the {\bf character lattice} of $G$ is \[ X(G) := \Hom_{\mathsf{GrpSch}_S}(G, \G_m). \] An element of $X(G)$ is called a {\bf character}.

nodes.title: Cocharacters of a group scheme
nodes.text: For a group scheme $G$ over $S$, the {\bf cocharacter lattice} of $G$ is \[ X^*(G) := \Hom_{\mathsf{GrpSch}_S}(\G_m, G). \] An element of $X^*(G)$ is called a {\bf cocharacter} or {\bf one-parameter subgroup}.

nodes.title: Character lattice of a diagonalisable group scheme
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain and $G$ be a commutative group. Then $X(\Spec R[G]) = G$.

nodes.title: Cocharacter lattice of a diagonalisable group scheme
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain and $G$ be a commutative group. Then $X^*(\Spec R[G]) = \Hom(G, \Z)$.

nodes.title: Character lattice of the torus
nodes.text: Let $G$ be a torus of dimension $n$ over a domain $R$. Then $X(G) = \Z^n$.

nodes.title: Cocharacter lattice of the torus
nodes.text: Let $G$ be a torus of dimension $n$ over a domain $R$. Then $X^*(G) = \Hom(\Z^n, \Z)$.

nodes.title: The character-cocharacter pairing
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain and $G$ a group scheme over $\Spec R$. Then there is a $\Z$-valued perfect pairing between $X(G)$ and $X^*(G)$.

nodes.title: The character-cocharacter pairing is perfect
nodes.text: The character-cocharacter pairing on a torus is perfect.

nodes.title: The image of a torus is a torus
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a domain. Let $T$ be a split torus over $R$. Let $G$ be a diagonalisable group scheme over $R$ and let $\phi: T \to G$ be a homomorphism. Then the (scheme theoretic) image of $\phi$ is a split torus over $R$ and the maps \[ T \xrightarrow{\hat{\phi}} \operatorname{im}\phi \xrightarrow{\iota} G \] are group homomorphisms, and $\hat{\phi}$ is fpqc. Furthermore, if $T = D_R(H), G = D_R(I), \phi = D_R(f)$ for $H$ a finitely generated free abelian group, $I$ an abelian group, $f : I \to H$ a group hom, then $\operatorname{im} \phi \cong D_R(\operatorname{im}(f))$.

nodes.title: A subgroup of a torus is a torus
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring of characteristic zero. Let $T$ be a split torus. If $H \subseteq T$ is a connected closed subgroup, then $H$ is a split torus.

nodes.title: Toric varieties
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T$ be a torus over $k$. A \emph{toric variety} structure on a scheme $X$ over $k$ consists the following data: \begin{itemize} \item a torus $T$ over $k$, \item a group action $T \times X \to X$ over $k$. \item a dominant open immersion $i : T \hookrightarrow X$ over $k$ that is $T$-equivariant. \end{itemize}

nodes.title: Torus morphisms, torus isomorphisms
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T_1, T_2$ be tori over $k$. Let $X_1, X_2$ be toric varieties with torus $T_1, T_2$ respectively. A \emph{toric morphism} from $X_1$ to $X_2$ is the data of a $k$-morphism $X_1 \to X_2$ and a $k$-group homomorphism $T_1 \to T_2$ that commute with the embeddings $T_1 \to X_1, T_2 \to X_2$ and the actions. A \emph{toric isomorphism} from $X_1$ to $X_2$ is the data of two isomorphisms $X_1 \cong X_2$ and $T_1 \cong T_2$ that commute with the embeddings $T_1 \to X_1, T_2 \to X_2$.

nodes.title: The diagonalisable group scheme of an affine monoid algebra is an affine toric variety
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $G$ be a finitely generated free abelian group. Let $M$ be an affine monoid with Grothendieck group $G$. Then $D_k(M)$ is an affine toric variety over $k$ with torus $D_k(G)$.

nodes.title: The character eigenspace
nodes.text: For a finite dimensional representation of a torus $T$ on $W$, the {\bf character eigenspace} of a character $\chi \in X(T)$ is \[ W_m = \{w\in W : t\cdot w = \chi(t)\text{ for all } t\in T \}. \]

nodes.title: Decomposition into character eigenspaces
nodes.text: The space decomposes into the direct sum of the character eigenspaces.
There is a torus action on the semigroup algebra $\bbC[M]$: given $t\in T_N$ and $f\in \bbC[M]$ define \[ t \cdot f = (p \mapsto f(t^{-1}p)). \]
Let $A \subseteq \bbC[M]$ be a stable subspace, then \[ A = \bigoplus_{\chi^m \in A} \bbC \cdot \chi^m. \]

nodes.title: Characters of a toric variety
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T$ be a torus over $k$. Let $V$ be a toric variety with torus $k$. The \emph{characters} $X(V)$ of $V$ are defined as the intersection of $X(T)$ with the image of the map $k[V] \to k[T]$ of coordinate rings induced by the embedding $T \hookrightarrow V$.

nodes.title: Characters of a toric variety are an affine monoid
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T$ be a torus over $k$. Let $V$ be a toric variety with torus $k$. Then $X(V)$ is an affine monoid.

nodes.title: Lattice ideal
nodes.text: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $G$ be a free abelian group and $M$ an affine monoid whose Grothendieck group is $G$. Let $L \le G$ be a sublattice. The \emph{lattice ideal} of $L$ is the $R$-ideal of $R[M]$ defined by \[ I_L := \langle X^\alpha - X^\beta | \alpha, \beta \in M, \alpha - \beta \in L\rangle. \]
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an affine monoid. A \emph{toric ideal} is a prime lattice $R$-ideal of $R[M]$.

nodes.title: An ideal is toric iff it is prime and generated by binomials
nodes.text: An ideal is toric if and only if it's prime and generated by binomials $X^\alpha - X^\beta$.

nodes.title: The vanishing ideal of a closed toric embedding
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $V$ be a toric variety over $k$. Let $i : V \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be a closed toric embedding. Then the vanishing ideal of $i$ is toric.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $s$ be an arbitrary indexing type, and $\MCA : s \to G$ an indexed family. Let $f'_\MCA$ be the map \begin{align*} \Z^{\oplus s} & \to G \\ e_i & \mapsto \MCA_i. \end{align*} and define $\Phi'_\MCA : D_S(G) \to \G_m^s$ as the image under $D_S$ of $f'_\MCA$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $s$ be an arbitrary indexing type, and $\MCA : s \to G$ an indexed family. Let $f_\MCA$ be the map \begin{align*} \N^{\oplus s} & \to G \\ e_i & \mapsto \MCA_i. \end{align*} and define $\Phi_\MCA : D_S(G) \to \mathbb A^s$ as the image under $D_S$ of $f_\MCA$.
$Y_\MCA$ is the scheme theoretic closure of $\im \Phi_\MCA$ in $\mathbb A^s$.
Let the base be $S=\Spec k$ for a field $k$, then $Y_\MCA$ is a toric variety.
The character lattice of the torus of $Y_\MCA$ is $\Z \MCA$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $s$ be an arbitrary indexing type, and $\MCA : s \to G$ an indexed family. Let $L$ be the kernel of $f'_\MCA : \Z^{\oplus s} \to G$. Then the ideal of the affine toric variety $Y_\MCA$ is \[ I(Y_\MCA) = I_L. \]
If $S$ is an affine monoid and $\mathcal A$ is a finite set generating $S$ as a monoid, then $\Spec \Bbbk[S] = Y_{\mathcal A}$.
The ideal of $Y_\MCA$ is a toric ideal.

nodes.title: Affine toric varieties come from affine monoids
nodes.text: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T$ be a torus over $k$. Let $V$ be a toric variety with torus $k$. Then there exists a torus isomorphism $V \cong D_k(X(V))$.
